title: Understanding the Loss Function
text: The loss function is given by $$L(theta)=y_i-\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(x_i\right)$$. This means the loss is the difference between the actual value $$y_i$$ and the predicted value $$\operatorname{f_{\theta}}\left(x_i\right)$$.

title: Gradient Descent Basics
text: Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm used to minimize a function by iteratively moving towards the steepest descent direction. In this case, we want to minimize the loss function.

title: Partial Derivatives
text: To perform gradient descent, we need to compute the partial derivatives of the loss function with respect to each parameter, $$\theta_0$$ and $$\theta_1$$.

title: Compute Partial Derivative with Respect to $$\theta_0$$
text: Calculate the partial derivative of the loss function L(theta) with respect to $$\theta_0$$.

title: Compute Partial Derivative with Respect to $$\theta_1$$
text: Calculate the partial derivative of the loss function L(theta) with respect to $$\theta_1$$.

title: Update Rule for Gradient Descent
text: The update rule for gradient descent is $$\theta_{new}=\theta_{old}-\alpha gradient$$, where alpha is the learning rate.

title: Update $$\theta_0$$
text: Using the update rule, calculate $${\theta_0}^1$$ given that $${\theta_0}^0=0$$ and the learning rate $$alpha=0.1$$.

title: Update $$\theta_1$$
text: Using the update rule, calculate $${\theta_1}^1$$ given that $${\theta_1}^0=0$$ and the learning rate $$alpha=0.1$$.
